一五一八年，胡安·迪亞茲作為胡安·德·格里哈爾瓦西班牙探險隊的成員，首次提及圖盧: In 1518 Juan Díaz, a member of Juan de Grijalva's Spanish expedition, first mentioned Tulum, and was among the first Europeans to find the site. In 1843 John Lloyd Stephens and Frederick Catherwood published the earliest detailed description in their book Incidents of Travel in Yucatan. Arriving by sea, they first saw a tall building that impressed them, very probably El Castillo at the site. They drew an accurate map of the site's walls, and Catherwood sketched El Castillo and other buildings. They also reported finding an Early Classic stela whose inscription is dated to the fifth century AD
圖盧姆遺址可能原名為薩瑪（Zama），意為「黎明之城」，因其面向日出方向。遺址位: The site of Tulum may originally have been called Zama, meaning "City of Dawn", because it faces the direction of sunrise. The site stands on cliffs facing the Caribbean. "Tulum" means "wall" or "ditch" in Yucatec Maya. The wall around the site let the stronghold of Tulum resist attack. Because it could use both land and sea trade routes, Tulum became an important trading hub, above all a centre for the obsidian trade. The murals and other works around the site show that Tulum was an important place of worship for the diving god or descending god.
圖盧姆風笛採用天然材料製作，管體主要由竹子、蘆葦或當地特有的木材製成。吹口部分可: The Tulum pipe is made from natural materials; the body is mainly bamboo, cane or a wood particular to the region. The mouthpiece may be worked from animal bone or horn. The inner bore is carefully smoothed to adjust pitch and tone quality. The surface may be decorated with natural dyes, and some parts are wrapped and reinforced with animal hide or plant fibre for durability and appearance.
圖盧姆風笛音色溫暖而粗獷，帶有明顯的民族特色。其音質略顯暗沉厚重，具有原始而深邃: The Tulum pipe has a warm, rugged timbre with a strongly local character. Its tone is a little dark and heavy, with a raw, deep texture. The range is fairly limited, mostly the middle and low register, and the tone is full and resonant. Because it is made of natural materials, the sound has obvious overtones and shifts through many layers. Next to a modern woodwind the timbre is coarser and more forceful; next to a European classical instrument such as the recorder it sounds more local and more primitive. The resonance carries, and in the open air it makes a long echo, well suited to a mysterious, desolate atmosphere.
圖盧姆（西班牙語發音：[tuˈlun]；猶卡坦瑪雅語：Tulu'um）是前哥倫布: Tulum (Spanish pronunciation: [tuˈlun]; Yucatec Maya: Tulu'um) is a walled city of the pre-Columbian Maya civilisation that served as the main port of Cobá, in the state of Quintana Roo, Mexico. The ruins stand on 12-metre (39 ft) cliffs on the Caribbean coast of the eastern Yucatán Peninsula. Tulum is one of the last cities the Maya built and lived in, and it flourished between the thirteenth and fifteenth centuries.
